dedupe_keys.name: enisa telecom security incidents annual reports eu incident reporting ciras

description: This policy evaluation series consists of ENISA's annual reports on major telecom security incidents in the European Union, based on the mandatory incident reports that operators send to national regulators and that regulators summarise to ENISA through the CIRAS platform. The latest report, Telecom Security Incidents 2024 (July 2025, 34 pages), covers 188 incidents from 26 EU Member States and two EFTA countries, up 20.5 percent from 156 incidents in 2023, while user hours lost fell from 3,906 million to 1,743 million; it analyses root-cause categories (system failures, human errors, natural phenomena, malicious actions, third-party failures), affected services and technical assets, and multiannual trends since 2012. Reporting was based on Article 13a of the Framework Directive from 2011 and Article 40 of the European Electronic Communications Code, and moves to the NIS2 Directive from October 2024. Coverage: EU and EEA countries, annual, aggregated and anonymised by incident; no country or operator is named. Format and access: free PDF reports under CC BY 4.0, with interactive statistics on the CIRAS portal. Caveats: thresholds for reporting differ by country; data are aggregated, so single incidents cannot be modelled; the series will change under NIS2. Simulation uses: calibration of outage frequencies and causes for resilience models, hazard exposure of telecom networks to weather and power failures, and evaluation of incident-reporting policy. Related records: the ENISA CIRAS incident data record, the FCC DIRS data and outage reviews such as Rogers 2022 and Optus 2023 give single-event detail.
